summary: Fraud/Intentional Misrepresentation, Negligence (incl. Negligence Per Se), IIED, Intentional Interference w/ Prospective Econ. Adv., Bane Act (§52.1), Declaratory Relief, UCL (§17200)

counts.title: Count 1 — Fraud / Intentional Misrepresentation (against all defendants): intake misrepresentations (March 2021); Akins group representation (November 2022); January 2024 group representation; June 2024 false homework statement; CTM 'partial homework' submissions to CDCR (November 2022–February 2026)

Count 2 — Negligence, including Negligence Per Se (against all defendants): PC §3008(d)(2) and 15 CCR §3574(f)(1) violated; special relationship under Giraldo; failure to maintain accurate homework records; false reporting of partial completion to CDCR

Count 3 — IIED (against all defendants): continued post-Dwyer blanket retention; false 'not completed' characterizations to CDCR; June 2024 false homework denial; August 2025 retaliatory CTM statements ('disruptive,' 'ringleader,' 'abhorrent,' 'acting job')

Count 4 — Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage (against all defendants): disruption of CDL carrier relationships (United Road, Keurig Dr Pepper, Tiger Lines LLC, US-1 Shorthaul, Lazer Spot Inc., Centerline Drivers); $109,408 documented 2022-2024 losses

Count 5 — Bane Act, Civ. Code §52.1 (against all defendants): interference with PC §3008(d)(2) and 15 CCR §3574(f)(1) rights through coercion; Palacios's August 2025 intimidation; $25,000 statutory damages per violation
Count 6 — Declaratory Relief: judicial declaration that HOPE's blanket retention policy is unlawful; permanent injunction requiring individualized assessment per published CASOMB criteria

Count 7 — UCL, Bus. & Prof. Code §17200 (against all defendants): blanket retention policy = unlawful business practice; false partial-homework reporting = unfair business practice; restitution of all fees wrongfully retained
